title: Changes you can and cannot undo

steps.say: Some changes can be undone. These are reversible changes, such as melting, freezing and dissolving.
Melted chocolate sets again when it cools. Salt can be got back from salty water by evaporation.
Other changes make new materials. These are irreversible changes, such as burning, cooking and rusting.
Signs of a new material include bubbles of gas, a new colour, a new smell, or heat and light.
Burning needs fuel, heat and oxygen. Take one of them away and the fire goes out.

figure.alt: The three things burning needs: fuel, heat and oxygen from the air.

steps.say: Iron rusts when it meets both water and oxygen. Paint and oil keep them away.

options.why: Melted ice can be frozen again.
The sugar can be got back by evaporating the water.
Frozen juice melts back into juice.

hints: An irreversible change makes a new material.
Ask which change you could never undo by cooling or heating.
Cross out the changes of state and the dissolving.
check.explanation: Frying an egg makes new materials, so it cannot be undone. Melting, dissolving and freezing are reversible.

check.prompt: Iron needs water and ___ to rust.
hints: Rust forms on bicycles left outside.
The second thing is a gas that fires also need.
It is the same gas we need to breathe.
check.explanation: Iron rusts when it reacts with water and oxygen from the air.
